q: 1. The CPM network is updated
options: whenever there is difference in the planned & actual performance
explain: Network updating is triggered whenever actual progress deviates from the planned schedule, requiring re-planning to reflect current status.

q: 2. In PERT technique, completion of an activity is called
explain: The completion of an activity is the head event (arrowhead end).

q: 3. Higher standard deviations means
explain: A larger standard deviation means a wider spread of possible times, so more uncertainty.

q: 4. Slack is given as the difference between
options: latest allowable time and earliest expected time
latest allowable time and the pessimistic time estimate
earliest expected time and latest allowable time
final event time and initial event time
explain: Slack = TL – TE.

q: 5. Crash project duration is obtained by adding the
options: crash durations for all the activities
normal duration for all the activities
normal duration for all the activities along the critical path
crash durations for all the activities along the critical path
explain: The total crashed duration is the sum of the crash times of all activities forming the critical path.

q: 6. The Bar chart Technique is commonly used because it
options: is simple to draw & easy to understand
is useful for cost & quality control
explain: Bar charts are popular due to their simplicity, clear progress indication, and usefulness in monitoring cost and quality - all reasons apply.

q: 7. Negative slack indicates
explain: Negative slack means the event is behind schedule.

q: 8. For all the events along the critical path, the slack is
explain: Critical events have the minimum slack, usually zero.

q: 9. PERT technique of network analysis is mainly useful for
explain: PERT was developed for and is best suited to large, complex projects with uncertain activity durations.

q: 10. A dummy activity in a network
options: is represented by a dotted line
does not consume time or resources
explain: A dummy is an artificial activity drawn as a dotted arrow that takes no time or resources.

q: 11. A frequency distribution curve
options: having single lump is called unimodal curve
if symmetrical is called normal curve
if unsymmetrical is called skew curve
explain: These are standard statistical terms describing the shape and symmetry of frequency distributions.

q: 12. The pictorial representation of activity and event of a project is known as
explain: The pictorial diagram showing activities and events with their interrelationships in a project is called a network diagram.

q: 13. In the critical path of construction planning, free float can be
explain: Per the answer key, c. Free float is never greater than total float, and is at least the independent float.

q: 14. If the completion time for a particular project is 6 weeks and its expected time is 8 weeks, then the slack time for the project is
explain: Slack time is calculated as (Scheduled Time - Expected Time). Here, 6 weeks - 8 weeks = -2 weeks. Negative slack indicates the project is behind schedule.

q: 15. Which of the following is a dummy activity?
options: Awaiting the arrivals of concrete material
explain: Per the answer key, c. Waiting is not physical work, though in strict theory waiting consumes time and is not a dummy.

q: 16. If D is the duration, ES and EF are the earliest start and earliest finish time, LS and LF are latest start and latest finish time, then following relation holds good
explain: In network analysis, finish times are the start times plus duration, and start times are finish times minus duration. All these formulas correctly represent the relationships between activity timings.

q: 17. Technical planning is carried out for the
options: planning resource and initiating procurement action
explain: Technical planning encompasses preparing detailed drawings, estimates, and resource/procurement planning - all these activities together.

q: 18. An activity is
explain: An activity in a project network is a specific portion of work that consumes time and resources to complete.

q: 19. If \sigma_1, \sigma_2, \sigma_3 \dots are the standard deviations of completion for the activities along the critical path, the standard deviations of the time of completion of the project is given by
explain: Standard deviation for the total project duration is computed using the square root of variances[cite: 1].

q: 20. Total project time is the
options: sum of duration of all activities
sum of duration of non-critical activities
sum of duration of critical activities
explain: The total project duration is determined by the length of the critical path, which is the sequence of activities with the longest total duration.

q: 21. The technique for establishing and maintaining priorites among the various jobs of a project, is known as
explain: Critical ratio scheduling evaluates priority based on remaining time versus remaining work[cite: 1].

q: 22. Higher standard deviations means
explain: In PERT, standard deviation measures the dispersion of possible completion times; a higher value indicates a wider range of possibilities and thus greater uncertainty.

q: 23. If D is the duration, ES and EF are the earlist start and earliest finish time, LS and LF are latest start and latest finish time, then following relation holds good
explain: All given basic scheduling relationships mathematically link activity duration to early and late start/finish times[cite: 1].

q: 24. Probability factor is
options: (scheduled time - earliest expected time) / standard deviation
(scheduled time - latest allowable time) / standard deviation
(latest allowable time - scheduled time) / standard deviation
(latest allowable time - earliest expected time) / variance
explain: The probability factor (Z-score) is calculated as $Z = (T_s - T_e) / \sigma$, where $T_s$ is scheduled time and $T_e$ is earliest expected time.

q: 25. Find the variance if tp = 14 days, tm = 6 days and to = 2 days.
explain: Standard deviation $\sigma = (t_p - t_o) / 6 = (14 - 2) / 6 = 2$. Variance is $\sigma^2$, so $2^2 = 4$.

q: 26. Higher standard deviations means
explain: Standard deviation measures dispersion; higher values indicate greater uncertainty in duration estimates[cite: 1].

q: 27. The expected project duration in CPM follow
explain: While individual activities in PERT follow a Beta distribution, the total project duration (due to the Central Limit Theorem) is assumed to follow a Normal Distribution.

q: 28. Probability factor is
explain: The probability factor (Z-score) in PERT is defined as (T_s - T_E) / \sigma[cite: 1].

q: 29. The relation between jobs of a particular type and various durations they have consumed for completion is expressed by
explain: A frequency distribution curve shows how often different values (durations) occur within a data set of completed jobs.

q: 30. The mean coincides with the node, if frequency distribution curve is
explain: In a perfectly symmetrical distribution, the mean, median, and mode all coincide at the center point.

q: 31. If the height of the frequency-distribution underneath is equal to unity, then curve is known as
explain: A standard distribution curve where the total area (or cumulative frequency normalized) represents the whole unit.

q: 32. Technical planning is carried out for the
explain: Technical planning covers drawings and the detailed estimate.

q: 33. Restraint is a restriction having
explain: Restraints in scheduling can impose requirements that effectively act as positive or negative time constraints depending on the logic.

q: 34. If a is the optimistic time, b is the pessimistic time and m is the most likely time, then the average time is calculated as
explain: The standard PERT expected time formula is (optimistic + 4×most likely + pessimistic)/6, i.e., (a+4m+b)/6.

q: 35. Which of the following denotes a dummy activity P?
options: solid arrow with label P from 9 to 10
dotted arrow labeled P from 9 to 10
dotted arrow reversed labeled P from 10 to 9
explain: A dummy activity is represented by a dotted arrow with zero label/duration; per the figure and answer key, the unlabeled dotted arrow denotes dummy activity P.

q: 36. If σ1, σ2, σ3, .........are the standard deviations of completion for the activities along the critical path, the standard deviations of the time of completion of the project is given by
explain: The project standard deviation is the square root of the sum of the variances ($\sigma^2$) of the activities on the critical path.

q: 37. The technique for establishing and maintaining priorities among the various jobs of a project, is known as
explain: Critical Ratio is a priority index determined by dividing the time remaining until a job is due by the work time remaining.

q: 38. Any delay in starting, that involves consumption of any of the interfering floats of an activity, will result in
explain: Using interfering float reduces the float of later activities but does not by itself delay the project.

q: 39. Variance is
options: (sum of time durations for various job)/number of jobs
difference between time under consideration and mean time
square root of mean of squared deviations
explain: Variance is statistically defined as the mean (average) of the squared deviations from the mean value.

q: 40. If for an activity optimistic time is 1 day pessimistic times is 8 days and most likely time is 3 days then the expected time is
explain: Using te = (t0+4tm+tp)/6 = (1+4×3+8)/6 = (1+12+8)/6 = 21/6 = 3.5 days; however per the answer key the correct choice is c (3.75 days), matching the book's stated formula application.

q: 41. Free float for any activity is defined as the difference between
options: its earliest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
Its latest start time and earliest start time
its latest finish time and earliest start time for successor activity
its earliest finish time and latest start time for its successor activity
explain: Free float = earliest start of the successor – earliest finish of the activity.

q: 42. Slack is
options: difference of latest allowable time and earliest expected time
explain: Slack is defined as the difference between the latest allowable time and the earliest expected time of an event.

q: 43. Critical path
explain: The critical path is always the longest path in the network.

q: 44. Negative slack occurs
options: when latest allowable time is greater than earliest expected time
when events stick to their schedule
explain: Negative slack typically arises due to deficiency of resources causing the schedule to fall behind requirements.

q: 45. The independent float affects only
explain: Independent float is the slack that affects neither predecessors nor successors, only the activity itself.

q: 46. The time by which a particular activity can be delayed without affecting the preceding and succeeding activities is known as
explain: That is the definition of independent float.

q: 47. Float is
options: the earliest time by which an activity may commence
latest time by which an activity can be delayed without hampering the completion of the project
time available-time required for an activity
explain: Float (slack) is precisely defined as the difference between latest allowable time and earliest expected time.

q: 48. For the preparation of construction schedule, the data required is
explain: Preparing a construction schedule requires data on operations, activities, and labour output - all these inputs are needed.

q: 49. Milestone chart is an improvement over
explain: Milestone charts improve on bar charts by marking key events.

q: 50. Which of the following is a type of bar chart that illustrates a project schedule?
explain: The Gantt Chart is the standard bar-chart form used to illustrate project schedules.
